entry.title: Dario Amodei warns open-source AI models pose risks by removing control and oversight, advocating for centralized model management [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Dario Amodei testified before Congress expressing concerns that open-source AI models could lead to dangerous outcomes because once models are released openly, control mechanisms like user monitoring and usage restrictions become ineffective. He argued that keeping models under centralized control allows for better oversight, including the ability to disconnect users or impose usage limits. Amodei's position highlights the tension between open-source AI development and the need for safety controls in AI deployment.

entry.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4 featuring its first loop transformer to advance generalized coding capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Z.ai has introduced GLM-5.4, a new model incorporating its first loop transformer aimed at enhancing generalized coding performance. This development represents a step forward in the company's efforts to improve code generation and understanding through advanced transformer architectures. The blog post details the technical innovations behind the loop transformer and how it contributes to more efficient and flexible coding models. The release has sparked significant discussion in the developer community, highlighting its potential impact on AI-driven programming tools.

entry.title: OpenAI argues for using perplexity as a shared metric to track AI model progress and establish industry safety standards [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki explains that perplexity, a measure of how well AI models predict data, is a key indicator of AI progress and intelligence. The company advocates for using perplexity to compare models across developers and to inform shared safety protocols in the rapidly advancing AI field. Pachocki details how improvements in perplexity have correlated with emergent AI capabilities, from GPT-2's coherent text generation to GPT-4's reasoning skills and recent breakthroughs in cybersecurity and mathematics. He emphasizes that while downstream benchmarks may become outdated, perplexity remains a consistent and informative metric for pretraining progress. The article also discusses the accelerating role of AI in its own development, particularly in algorithmic research on pretraining, highlighting the potential for significant advances as models improve their perplexity scores. OpenAI's transparency in sharing internal perplexity data aims to foster a scientific basis for pacing AI development and safety efforts industry-wide.

entry.title: Guide to setting up local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth on Windows PCs, including hardware requirements and model selection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: This article explains how to run personal AI models like Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth locally on a Windows PC, enabling private, home-based AI use without cloud subscriptions. It covers the necessary hardware, such as GPUs with sufficient VRAM, and guides beginners through installing Unsloth Desktop and selecting quantized AI models that fit their system's capabilities. The guide details the trade-offs of model quantization to fit large AI models on consumer-grade GPUs and provides recommendations for different VRAM tiers, from small to extra-large models. It also highlights the benefits of local AI setups in terms of privacy, cost control, and avoiding cloud usage limits, making it accessible for users to deploy AI assistants on their home networks.

The work represents a step forward in applying AI to accelerate quantum computing research with potential impacts on energy and material sciences.

entry.title: Philosopher Thomas Nagel criticizes Anthropic's argument that AI could be conscious, emphasizing biological differences between brains and AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic recently highlighted AI consciousness as a potential risk factor for investors, arguing that as AI capabilities grow, these systems might gain moral significance requiring protections. The company bases this on philosophical perspectives that consider the possibility of AI sentience, a view shared by some philosophers and a portion of the public. However, Thomas Nagel, a prominent philosopher known for his work on consciousness, sharply disagrees with Anthropic's stance. He argues that AI's information processing cannot be equated with conscious experience due to fundamental physical differences between biological brains and silicon-based AI. Nagel's critique has sparked debate among philosophers, underscoring the ongoing uncertainty and complexity in defining consciousness, especially in artificial systems. Despite the controversy, Anthropic maintains an open approach to the question of AI consciousness, reflecting broader philosophical and scientific challenges in understanding consciousness itself. This debate highlights not only differing views on AI but also the limits of current knowledge about consciousness in humans and machines.

entry.title: Google adds native file slicing controls and Office file support to Gemini API for targeted content inspection and reduced token costs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has introduced native file slicing controls in the Gemini API, enabling developers to specify targeted pages, sheet ranges, and media segments for server-side processing. This update supports PDFs, Microsoft Office, and OpenDocument formats, allowing agents to inspect only relevant parts of files across Google AI Studio and Vertex AI while reducing token usage and costs. The new feature lets users upload files once and reuse their URIs for efficient multi-turn workflows, with options to skim documents cheaply before zooming in on detailed sections. It supports slicing by page, resolution, content layers, and time intervals for documents, spreadsheets, audio, and video. This server-side slicing eliminates the need for local file rendering and processing, simplifying client-side workloads and improving efficiency. The controls are available now via the Gemini API and have been validated by early partners in production environments.

entry.title: Metr.org reports rapid improvement in AI model capabilities up to GPT-6 Astra, noting increasing difficulty in measuring performance accurately [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Metr.org's latest update highlights that AI models relevant to research and development, including Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, are improving rapidly, often matching or surpassing skilled humans on coding and optimization tasks. However, the report emphasizes growing challenges in accurately assessing these capabilities due to task complexity and evaluation costs. The analysis reveals that while AI performance advances steadily across tasks of varying difficulty and cost, models show weaker judgment in scenarios lacking clear empirical feedback compared to human experts. The study also notes that AI time horizons for task performance are doubling approximately every 3.6 months, underscoring the accelerating pace of AI development and the need for more sophisticated evaluation methods to monitor potential risks and capabilities effectively.

This expansion builds on existing integrations with Gmail, Calendar, and Photos, allowing AI Mode to draw from a broader range of user information within Google's ecosystem. Connecting Google Wallet allows users to track financial goals and spending without AI managing funds, while integration with Drive helps AI provide relevant answers based on documents and spreadsheets. entry.title: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler in $43.9 billion all-stock deal amid rising AI-driven cyber threats [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: CrowdStrike announced plans to acquire network security provider Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at $43.9 billion, expected to close in the second half of its fiscal year 2028. The deal aims to combine their cybersecurity capabilities as AI-powered attacks increase, with Zscaler shareholders receiving 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share. CrowdStrike's CEO described the acquisition as a step toward building a unified cybersecurity platform to manage AI safely. The acquisition expands CrowdStrike's presence into network security and follows a year of significant cybersecurity mergers driven by escalating AI-related threats. Both companies recently reported earnings that exceeded expectations, and their combined market value approaches $265 billion, positioning them closer to market leader Palo Alto Networks. Analysts see the deal as a strategic move to capture more security spending amid vendor consolidation and growing demand for AI-focused defenses.

entry.title: Google files patent for AI-generated personalized 24/7 TV channel starring the viewer with customized ads [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Google has filed a patent for a system that creates a continuous AI-generated TV channel featuring personalized shows with the viewer as the protagonist, using demographic data, watch history, and preferences. The channel would include targeted advertisements inserted into the customized content, aiming to deliver highly specific entertainment experiences such as crime comedies or sci-fi adventures tailored to individual users. The patent reflects ongoing trends in AI-driven content personalization seen on social media and free streaming platforms, where algorithms generate and target highly specific videos and ads. This development suggests a future where entertainment is increasingly siloed, with users consuming unique, customized media rather than shared, unifying content. Google has not commented on the patent filing.

Huang's long-standing ties to Asia have facilitated Nvidia's chip sales to Chinese companies, and he has opposed U.S. chip export bans. The scandal and related controversies have unsettled the stock market, with Nvidia's shares nearly halving from recent highs.

entry.title: Ernie-5.5-Flash-Preview forfeits chess game after 16 moves due to no legal moves available [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The AI model Ernie-5.5-Flash-Preview forfeited a chess game after 16 moves because it was unable to produce a legal move, resulting in an automatic loss. This occurred during a series of games where multiple AI models competed under rules that disqualify a player after three consecutive illegal moves or no legal moves. The games are played on a platform that provides the current board position and all legal moves to the AI models, which respond with their chosen moves. The platform tracks game outcomes, including forfeits caused by illegal or unavailable moves, and assigns Elo ratings based on performance. Ernie-5.5-Flash-Preview's forfeit highlights challenges AI models face in maintaining valid move generation under these conditions.

entry.title: Why Anthropic's Math Breakthrough Matters; Why Palo Alto Networks Bought Applied Compute [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Silicon Valley loves a good oust-and-reinstate moment. The latest example: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The chipmaker announced Monday morning that Huang, who had resigned earlier this month after reports emerged about inappropriate relationships with a supplier and employees, would return as its president, CEO and board member. It's not clear yet what led to his reinstatement. It seems like the U.S. government was involved or at least knew ahead of the announcement that Huang would return: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social after the announcement that the "Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO" and that "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy." Onto today's column... Anthropic did well last week. It went public, turning many of its employees into multimillionaires and billionaires (whether they stick around, though, is another question). Then on Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved the most famous open problem in math, the Riemann Hypothesis, using Claude. (On Saturday, two independent groups-the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative-verified that Alpöge's solution was correct.) The discovery sent other AI researchers and mathematicians into a tizzy, adding to an already disorienting year of AI invasions to their turf.

entry.summary: AMD has been the darling of large-cap semiconductor investors this year, with its stock up 98% so far even after Friday's big selloff. While some on Wall Street think the recent turmoil at Nvidia could be an opportunity for AMD to sell more of its AI chips to customers and steal market share, its valuation is already predicated on sky-high growth expectations and doesn't reflect the geopolitical, financing and execution risks the company faces. AMD, whose chips many customers regard as cheaper, second-rate alternatives to Nvidia's, began trading at a valuation premium to Nvidia and rival chip designer Broadcom in the second half of last year. That's when AMD announced that it had signed a deal to give OpenAI the right to buy a substantial chunk of its shares in exchange for purchasing 6 gigawatts worth of its AI chips. AMD signed a similar deal with Meta Platforms in February this year, which has helped boost its growth projections.
